  newId(): string

  validateCard(input, options?): { ok: true, value: { title, description, assignee, column, position } } | { ok: false, error: string, errors?: { [field]: string } }
    Accepts: { title, description?, assignee?, column?, position? }
    Rules:
      - title: trimmed, non-empty string, max 80 characters (required)
      - description: string, default ''
      - assignee: string, default ''
      - column: must be in COLUMNS, default 'todo'
      - position: non-negative integer
    options.partial (boolean, default false): when true, all fields are optional (for PATCH use).
    Returns { ok: true, value: normalised-card-fields } on success.
    Returns { ok: false, error: string, errors?: {field: message} } on failure (never throws).

  validateMove(input): { ok: true, value: { column, position } } | { ok: false, error: string }
    Accepts: { column, position }
    Rules: column in COLUMNS; position non-negative integer.
    Returns same ok/error shape (never throws).

Since Droid explicitly marks ownership/columns/exports as negotiable and Claude's server is the producer of the API, Claude owns the file. Droid must not produce shared/cards.js. The contract resolves all differences in Claude's favour for format/style and Droid's favour for richer card fields and the 80-char title limit (board.limits item 12 requires 80).

proposal.contractText:
Owner: project-2-droid (droid).

File: store/index.js
Module format: ESM (package.json type:"module" in store/, or .mjs extension).
Claude's server/ must import it via dynamic import() or a thin ESM entry file.

Exported functions (all async, all named exports):

  list(): Promise<Card[]>
    Returns all cards sorted by column then position.

  get(id: string): Promise<Card | null>
    Returns card or null if not found.

  create(input: { id: string, title: string, description?: string, assignee?: string, column?: string }): Promise<Card>
    Appends card at end of column; position assigned automatically.

  update(id: string, patch: { title?, description?, assignee? }): Promise<Card | null>
    Returns updated card, or null if id unknown (do NOT throw).

  move(id: string, column: string, position: number): Promise<Card | null>
    Moves card; reorders positions to stay contiguous 0-based.
    Returns updated card, or null if id unknown (do NOT throw).

  remove(id: string): Promise<boolean>
    Returns true if deleted, false if id unknown (do NOT throw).

  on(event: 'change', listener: (payload) => void): void
  off(event: 'change', listener: (payload) => void): void
    Change payload: { type: 'card.created'|'card.updated'|'card.moved'|'card.deleted', card: Card }
    Emitted after successful persistence.

Card object shape: { id: string, title: string, description: string, assignee: string, column: string, position: number }
  description and assignee always present (default '').

Persistence: atomic JSON file writes; default path configurable but defaults to store/data.json.

Non-negotiable (Claude's requirement): unknown-id operations return null or false, never throw NOT_FOUND.
proposal.rationale: Claude requires the store to be CommonJS with synchronous functions, returning null/false for unknown ids rather than throwing, and a card shape of exactly {id,title,column,position}. Droid produces an ESM async store with a factory function, async methods, throws NOT_FOUND for missing ids, and a richer card shape. These are deeply incompatible: module format, sync vs async, error signalling, factory vs direct export, and card shape all conflict. Claude's requirement is explicitly marked non-negotiable on card shape and null/false returns. However, async and ESM are better fits for file I/O and for Droid's change-event model. The contract resolves by making Droid the store owner (it is the producer), adopting ESM async, richer card shape, and change events, but requires Droid to return null/false instead of throwing for unknown ids (honouring Claude's non-negotiable) and to export functions directly (no factory) so Claude's require()-wrapping shim works. Claude must use a thin CommonJS compatibility shim in server/ to import the ESM store.

proposal.contractText:
Transport: Server-Sent Events (SSE) only. No WebSocket endpoint.

Route: GET /api/events
  Response headers:
    Content-Type: text/event-stream
    Cache-Control: no-cache
    Connection: keep-alive

Event protocol (each event is a standard SSE frame):

1. On client connect:
   event: snapshot
   data: <JSON array of all Card objects, sorted by column then position>

2. After any create / update / move / delete mutation completes (post-persistence):
   event: cards
   data: <JSON array of all Card objects, sorted by column then position>

   (Clients replace their entire local state with this array; no delta processing needed.)

3. Heartbeat (keepalive, no event name):
   : heartbeat
   Sent every 15 seconds.

Reconnect: browsers auto-reconnect SSE; on reconnect the server sends a fresh 'snapshot' event, so no separate refresh call is needed.

Card object shape in both event types: { id, title, description, assignee, column, position } (matches board.api contract).
proposal.rationale: Claude produces SSE on GET /api/events with a 'snapshot' event on connect then full-array 'cards' events after mutations. Codex assumes WebSocket /ws as primary and treats SSE as a fallback where the UI refetches GET /api/board on each event. Droid defers transport ownership to Claude. The conflict is WebSocket vs SSE transport and snapshot-vs-refetch update model. The contract standardises on Claude's SSE approach (Node built-ins only makes WS harder without npm; SSE is simpler) and clarifies the snapshot event so Codex can drop its refetch approach—the snapshot event carries full state on connect and on reconnect.

proposal.contractText:
File: store/index.js
Module format: ESM (the store/ directory has its own package.json with {"type":"module"}, or the file uses .mjs extension). The server/ layer imports it via ESM import.

Store card shape (internal, persisted):
  { id: string, title: string, column: string, position: number }
  description and assignee are NOT stored here; the API layer manages them separately.

Factory function (default export or named):
  async function createStore({ filePath: string }): Promise<Store>
    Opens / creates the JSON file at filePath. Returns a Store instance.
    The JSON file holds an array of { id, title, column, position } objects.
    Writes are atomic (write to a temp file, then rename).

Store instance methods (all async):

  list(): Promise<Card[]>
    Returns all cards sorted by column then position.
    Card shape: { id, title, column, position }.

  get(id: string): Promise<Card | null>
    Returns the card or null if not found.

  create(input: { id: string, title: string, column: string }): Promise<Card>
    Appends card at end of column (position = max existing position in column + 1, or 0).
    Returns { id, title, column, position }.

  move(id: string, column: string, position: number): Promise<Card | null>
    Moves card to the given column at the given position.
    Keeps positions contiguous (0-based) within each column after the move.
    Returns updated { id, title, column, position }, or null if id is unknown.

  update(id: string, patch: { title?: string }): Promise<Card | null>
    Updates only the title field (the only mutable non-positional field in the store).
    Returns updated card, or null if id is unknown.
    (column/position changes must go through move().)

  remove(id: string): Promise<boolean>
    Deletes the card. Resequences positions in its former column to remain contiguous.
    Returns true if deleted, false if id was unknown.

Change events (EventEmitter interface on the Store instance):
  store.on('change', listener)
  store.off('change', listener)
  Payload emitted after persistence completes:
    { type: 'card.created' | 'card.moved' | 'card.updated' | 'card.deleted', card: Card }
  The server/ layer subscribes to broadcast SSE events.

Error handling:
  Unknown id: return null (for get, move, update) or false (for remove). Never throw for missing id.
  I/O or parse errors: throw a native Error.

Positions:
  Always 0-based integers, contiguous per column. The store enforces this on every mutation.
proposal.rationale: Claude (the API layer, item 6) rejected P5 because it requires card shape exactly {id,title,column,position} — no description/assignee — and null/false returns for unknown ids rather than throws. However, the board.api contract (P2) and board.validation contract (P4) both define the full Card shape {id,title,description,assignee,column,position}. The store is an internal persistence module whose card shape need not match the wire shape: the API layer can add description/assignee defaults when it reads from the store. The revised contract therefore uses the minimal shape claude requires in the store file itself, while the API layer remains responsible for enriching cards to the full wire shape. Droid's async ESM approach is retained (claude accepted async ESM and null/false returns). The update() function is dropped per claude's rejection; PATCH is handled by the API calling move() and/or create()+remove() as needed, or via a targeted update that only touches column/position. To satisfy PATCH /api/cards/:id fully (title, description, assignee changes), a minimal update(id, patch) that only accepts {title?,column?,position?} is added — description and assignee are NOT stored in the store file, keeping the store card shape exactly as claude requires. The API layer holds description/assignee in a separate in-memory or sidecar structure, or re-validates and re-derives them. Actually, reconsidering: the cleanest resolution that respects claude's non-negotiable (card shape exactly {id,title,column,position}) while still supporting the full wire Card is to store only {id,title,column,position} and have the API maintain description/assignee in a separate in-memory map. The store contract below reflects this.

    description: string,   // default ""
    assignee: string,       // default ""
    column: string,
    position: number,
    labels: { name: string, color: string }[]  // default []
  }
  All seven fields are persisted durably in store/index.js (no API-side sidecar).
  Old cards without a labels field are returned with labels: [].

Columns (ordered): ["todo", "doing", "done"]

Allowed label colors (fixed server-side palette):
  ["red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple", "pink", "gray"]
  (Discoverable via GET /api/board; UI must not hard-code the palette.)

WIP limit:
  The server is configured with a doing-column WIP limit (numeric or null for unlimited).
  Default: null (unlimited) unless configured.
  Exposed read-only to clients; never modifiable via the API.

Routes (all bodies and responses are application/json):

1. GET /api/board
   Response 200:
   {
     columns: ["todo", "doing", "done"],
     cards: Card[],            // sorted by column then position
     limits: { doing: number | null },
     labelColors: string[]     // the allowed color palette
   }
   Server derives cards from store.list().

2. GET /api/cards
   Response 200: Card[]  (sorted by column then position)

3. POST /api/cards
   Request body: { title: string (required), column?: string, description?: string, assignee?: string, labels?: { name: string, color: string }[] }
   labels defaults to [] if omitted.
   Each label must have name (non-empty string) and color (one of the allowed palette values).
   If column is 'doing' and the doing WIP limit is set and currently reached, respond:
     Error 400: { error: "WIP limit reached for column 'doing'", errors: { column: "doing column is full" } }
   Response 201: Card
   Error 400: { error: string, errors?: { [field]: string } }

4. PATCH /api/cards/:id
   Request body (any subset): { column?: string, position?: number, description?: string, assignee?: string, title?: string, labels?: { name: string, color: string }[] }
   If column and/or position are present, the card is moved; position is the final zero-based index in the target column after source removal.
   If the target column is 'doing' (and it differs from the card's current column) and the WIP limit is reached, respond:
     Error 400: { error: "WIP limit reached for column 'doing'", errors: { column: "doing column is full" } }
   Same-column reorder (column unchanged or equal to current) is never blocked by the WIP limit.
   If only title/description/assignee/labels are present, the card is updated in place.
   labels, if supplied, replaces the card's entire labels array; each entry validated as above.
   Response 200: Card
   Error 404: { error: string }   (unknown id)
   Error 400: { error: string, errors?: { [field]: string } }   (invalid fields)

5. DELETE /api/cards/:id
   Response 204  (no body)
   Error 404: { error: string }

All other errors: { error: string }

WIP limit check is atomic with the store write: server reads current column occupancy from store.list() immediately before calling store.create() or store.move(), inside a request-scoped lock or sequential async queue to prevent races.

  Old cards without a labels field are returned with labels: [].

Allowed label colors (fixed server-side palette):
  ["red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple", "pink", "gray"]
  (Discoverable via GET /api/board; UI must not hard-code the palette.)

  The server is configured with a doing-column WIP limit (numeric or null for unlimited).
  Default: null (unlimited) unless configured.
  Exposed read-only to clients; never modifiable via the API.

Routes (all bodies and responses are application/json):

1. GET /api/board
   Response 200:
   {
     columns: ["todo", "doing", "done"],
     cards: Card[],            // sorted by column then position
     limits: { doing: number | null },
     labelColors: string[]     // the allowed color palette
   }
   Server derives cards from store.list().

2. GET /api/cards
   Response 200: Card[]  (sorted by column then position)

3. POST /api/cards
   Request body: { title: string (required), column?: string, description?: string, assignee?: string, labels?: { name: string, color: string }[] }
   labels defaults to [] if omitted.
   Each label must have name (non-empty string) and color (one of the allowed palette values).
   If column is 'doing' and the doing WIP limit is set and currently reached, respond:
     Error 400: { error: "WIP limit reached for column 'doing'", errors: { column: "doing column is full" } }
   Response 201: Card
   Error 400: { error: string, errors?: { [field]: string } }

4. PATCH /api/cards/:id
   Request body (any subset): { column?: string, position?: number, description?: string, assignee?: string, title?: string, labels?: { name: string, color: string }[] }
   If column and/or position are present, the card is moved; position is the final zero-based index in the target column after source removal.
   If the target column is 'doing' (and it differs from the card's current column) and the WIP limit is reached, respond:
     Error 400: { error: "WIP limit reached for column 'doing'", errors: { column: "doing column is full" } }
   Same-column reorder (column unchanged or equal to current) is never blocked by the WIP limit.
   If only title/description/assignee/labels are present, the card is updated in place.
   labels, if supplied, replaces the card's entire labels array; each entry validated as above.
   Response 200: Card
   Error 404: { error: string }   (unknown id)
   Error 400: { error: string, errors?: { [field]: string } }   (invalid fields)
